title: API bearer key hard-coded in a client script served to every visitor
evidence: api.js is loaded by index.html:25 as a plain script; the key is sent as Authorization on every request (api.js:6, 11). README.md:6 says the key never leaves the server.
failing_case: Any visitor opens DevTools or views api.js, copies the key and calls POST /v1/refunds with it, moving money without using the dashboard.
remediation: Move the key to a server-side proxy that authenticates the user and enforces refund limits; rotate the shipped key.

title: Customer name, id, total and status are interpolated into innerHTML unescaped (stored XSS)
evidence: Drove index.html in Playwright with the API stubbed: a customer named on the visible page set window.XSS to 1. The same string sink is used for o.id, o.total and o.status. Also innerHTML += inside a loop re-parses the whole tbody per row.
failing_case: A customer registers with the name ; any agent who opens the dashboard runs the script in a page that holds the refund key (api.js:3) and can issue refunds.
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent (or one escape function applied at every interpolation) and set the whole tbody once.

title: The Refund control is a span: not focusable, no role, unreachable by keyboard and screen reader
evidence: index.html:19 uses a span with an onclick set in app.js:49. A span has no tab stop and no button role (WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2, both level A). Traced.
failing_case: Tab through the page: focus goes Search, Status, checkboxes, Prev, Next and skips Refund selected. Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot refund at all.
remediation: Use <button type="button" class="refund">; keep the visible focus style and disable it while nothing is selected.

quote: - **Fully accessible:** meets WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44 px touch targets (criterion 2.5.5).
title: README claims WCAG 2.1 AA that the page demonstrably fails, and cites 2.5.5 as AA
evidence: See the contrast, focus, label, keyboard and motion findings. 2.5.5 Target Size is AAA in WCAG 2.1, not AA; the buttons are 12 px text with 2px 4px padding.
failing_case: A buyer relies on the claim for a procurement or legal accessibility statement; the product fails 1.4.3, 2.1.1, 2.4.7, 4.1.2.
remediation: Remove the claim until measured with an audit; if kept, state the level correctly and fix the failures.

quote: - **Pricing:** the Team plan is $15 per seat; 12 seats on annual billing at 20% off is $1,440 a year.
title: Pricing arithmetic is wrong
evidence: If $15 is per seat per month: 15 x 12 seats x 12 months = $2,160; 20% off = $1,728. If $15 is per seat per year: 15 x 12 = $180; 20% off = $144. $1,440 matches neither (computed).
failing_case: A customer is quoted $1,440 when the stated price gives $1,728 (or $144).
remediation: State the billing period of the $15 and correct the total, or compute it from one source.

quote: fetch(`${API_BASE}/refunds`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: "[redacted]" + API_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ ids }) });
title: refund() does not await the request and returns {ok:true} regardless of the outcome
evidence: api.js:11-12: the fetch promise is neither awaited nor caught, then `return { ok: true }`. Driven: with the refunds endpoint answering 500 the UI still showed 'Refunded 2 orders!'. An empty selection also shows 'Refunded 0 orders!'.
failing_case: The API is down or rejects the call (402, 500, offline): the agent sees a success toast, believes customers were refunded, and an unhandled rejection is logged.
remediation: await the fetch, check res.ok, return the real result, and show the error with a retry on failure; do not send an empty list.

title: Pagination is off by one: page 1 skips the first 10 orders; Prev goes to page -1 and Next past the end
evidence: Driven: with 25 orders page 1 shows C11.., labelled 'Page 1 of 2'. Prev twice showed 'Page -1 of 2' with 0 rows; six Next clicks showed 'Page 5 of 2' with 0 rows. app.js:47-48 have no bounds; app.js:34 uses Math.floor so 25 orders gives 2 pages (3 are needed) and 5 orders gives 0.
failing_case: Load any list: orders 1-10 are never reachable. With 25 orders the last 5 are on a page numbered 3, but the label says 2 pages.
remediation: Use (page-1)*PAGE_SIZE, Math.max(1, Math.ceil(n/PAGE_SIZE)) pages, clamp Prev and Next, disable the buttons at the ends.

title: Order status is shown only as a coloured dot with no text
evidence: app.js:32 emits an empty span; styles.css:17 colours it green, red or yellow (#3c3, #c33, #cc3). No text, title or aria-label. WCAG 1.4.1 (A) and 1.1.1. The dots also fail 3:1 on white (yellow #cc3 is about 1.9:1). Traced.
failing_case: A colour-blind user cannot tell paid from refunded; a screen-reader user hears nothing in the Status column. The search box also cannot filter by it.
remediation: Print the status word next to the dot (or instead), with a text colour that meets 4.5:1.

title: Selection only ever grows: unchecking does not remove an id, duplicates accumulate, and refunds hit orders the user deselected
evidence: Driven: checked orders 11 and 12, unchecked 12; selected stayed ['11','12'] and the refund toast said 'Refunded 2 orders!'. selected is never cleared after a refund or a reload. Re-render (app.js:30) also drops the visible checked state while selected keeps ids.
failing_case: Tick A and B, untick B, click Refund: B is refunded. Tick A twice across re-renders: A is sent twice. Money is refunded for an order the agent deliberately excluded.
remediation: Keep selection as a Set keyed by id, add on check and delete on uncheck, restore checked state on render, clear after a confirmed refund.

title: Load has no error handling and applies responses out of order, and fires one request per keystroke
evidence: app.js:45 oninput = load with no debounce; api.js:7 returns res.json() without checking res.ok. Any 4xx/5xx or network failure becomes an unhandled rejection and a blank/stale UI; a slow early response can overwrite a later one.
failing_case: User types 'ann': request for 'a' is slow and returns last; the table shows results for 'a' while the box says 'ann'. On a 500 the page silently shows old data with no message.
remediation: Debounce input, abort the previous request with AbortController (or ignore stale sequence numbers), check res.ok and show an error with a retry.

title: Refund fires immediately with no confirmation (README says refunds are confirmed) and also fires with an empty selection
evidence: README.md:9 states 'Refunds are confirmed before they are sent'. app.js:49-52 calls refund(selected) directly: no confirm dialog, no summary, no undo, no check that selected is non-empty. Traced.
failing_case: Click Refund selected with nothing selected: a POST with ids [] is sent and the toast says 'Refunded 0 orders!'. With orders selected, one click sends the money back with no confirmation step.
remediation: Disable the button until something is selected, show a confirm step naming the count and total, and send only after it; or fix the README.

quote: if (r.ok) { const t = document.getElementById("toast"); t.textContent = "Refunded " + selected.length + " orders!"; t.style.display = "block"; }
title: Toast reports an unverified refund, never hides, is not announced, and uses a count of selected ids rather than refunded orders
evidence: Driven: toast stayed display:block after 500 response and after a second click. No timeout or dismiss anywhere in app.js. #toast in index.html:23 has no role=status/aria-live. '1 orders' grammar.
failing_case: Screen reader user clicks Refund and hears nothing; sighted user sees a success message that stays forever whatever the server said.
remediation: Drive the toast from the confirmed response, add role="status", auto-hide or dismiss, and a separate error toast with role="alert".

title: Search box and status select have no accessible label; table checkboxes are unnamed
evidence: index.html:17-18 use placeholder only and no <label>/aria-label; app.js:32 renders each checkbox with no label, and the first <th> is empty (index.html:21). Status dot is colour only (styles.css:17), no text.
failing_case: Screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'combo box' and 'checkbox' with no name; user cannot tell which order a checkbox refunds or which status a dot means; colour-blind users cannot tell paid from refunded (1.4.1, 1.3.1, 4.1.2).
remediation: Add <label> or aria-label to the inputs, aria-label="Select order {id}" on checkboxes, and show status as text with the colour.

title: Text contrast fails WCAG 1.4.3 in several places
evidence: Computed ratios: #aaa on #fff 2.32:1 (.lbl, and `button` at styles.css:18); #c7c2f0 on #6366f1/#8b5cf6 2.64/2.50:1 (.eyebrow, styles.css:4, 11 px); #fff on #8b5cf6 4.23:1 (.refund, styles.css:12). All need 4.5:1 for this size.
failing_case: A low-vision user cannot read REVENUE/ORDERS labels, the Prev/Next buttons, or the eyebrow.
remediation: Use #595959 or darker for labels and buttons, a pale-on-dark colour at 4.5:1 or more for the eyebrow, and a darker purple for the refund button; raise 11 px text.

title: Fixed 1000 px table forces sideways scroll on phones; cards keep three columns
evidence: Driven at 390 px: document scrollWidth 1024. styles.css:6 keeps repeat(3, 1fr) at any width; styles.css:15 clips the customer name at 120 px with no ellipsis or title; 6 px cell padding gives targets well under 44 px. Prev/Next are 12 px text buttons.
failing_case: On a 390 px phone the whole page scrolls horizontally and long customer names are cut off with no indication.
remediation: Use width:100% with an overflow-x wrapper or stacked rows below ~640 px, one-column cards, text-overflow: ellipsis.

quote: button { border: 0; background: none; color: #aaa; padding: 2px 4px; font-size: 12px; }
title: Prev and Next buttons are #aaa 12px text on the cream page (about 2.1:1), with no border or background to mark them as controls
evidence: #aaa (L 0.402) on #F4F1EA (L about 0.88) gives about 2.1:1; WCAG 1.4.3 (AA) and 1.4.11 (non-text contrast). The buttons are about 12 px tall (padding 2px 4px), so they are also a tiny touch target. Traced.
failing_case: The pager is barely visible and looks like disabled text; a user on a phone must hit a roughly 40x20 px target.
remediation: Give the buttons a border or filled background, text at 4.5:1 or better, 14-16 px type and padding that yields a target of at least 24 px (44 px preferred).

title: Focus outline removed from every control with no replacement
evidence: No :focus-visible rule anywhere in styles.css. Also Prev/Next buttons are #aaa 12px with no background or border, so they look like text (styles.css:18).
failing_case: Keyboard user tabbing through search, status and Prev/Next cannot see where focus is (WCAG 2.4.7 AA).
remediation: Delete the rule or replace it with a visible :focus-visible outline of at least 3:1 contrast.

quote: - **Secure:** the API key never leaves the server.
title: README says the API key never leaves the server; it is in a public client script
evidence: api.js:3 holds the key, loaded by index.html:25 in the browser.
failing_case: Anyone reading the README trusts the key is private; it is world-readable at /api.js.
remediation: Fix the architecture (server proxy) or delete the claim.

title: Every keystroke fires a request with no debounce, and late responses overwrite newer ones
evidence: load() awaits getOrders and then assigns the shared `orders` (app.js:41). There is no request id, abort or stale check, and getOrders fetches the whole list each time.
failing_case: Type 'ann' quickly: the response for 'a' arrives after the response for 'ann'. The table and stats show results for 'a' while the box reads 'ann'.
remediation: Debounce input about 250 ms and use an AbortController (or a sequence counter) so only the latest request may update state.

title: README says refunds are confirmed before sending; the money-moving control is an unconfirmed, non-focusable span
evidence: README.md:9 claims confirmation. app.js:49-52 calls refund() immediately on click, with no confirm dialog. The control is a span: no tabindex, no role, no key handler, so keyboard and screen reader users cannot reach it (WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2).
failing_case: A keyboard-only user cannot refund at all (main task blocked); a mouse user who mis-clicks sends the refund with no confirmation or undo.
remediation: Use a real <button type="button">, show a confirm step naming the number and total of orders, and disable it when nothing is selected.

title: '10,000 orders instantly' is unsupported and contradicted by the code
evidence: app.js:32 does innerHTML += per row, and renderTable renders only 10 rows; renderStats loops all orders per keystroke with a fetch per keystroke (app.js:45). No benchmark in the repo.
failing_case: No measurement exists; with 10,000 orders every keystroke refetches and reprocesses all 10,000 and nothing paginates server-side.
remediation: Measure and state the number, or remove the claim; paginate on the server.

title: Search text is put into the query string without encoding
evidence: query comes straight from the #q input (app.js:39). A value like `x&status=refunded#` changes or truncates the request.
failing_case: Search 'Smith & Sons' sends q=Smith & Sons: the server sees q=Smith and a bogus parameter ' Sons'; '#' truncates the rest of the URL.
remediation: Build the URL with URLSearchParams or encodeURIComponent on each value.

title: getOrders never checks the HTTP status; load() has no catch, so a failure leaves a stale or broken page with no message
evidence: api.js:6-7 returns res.json() whatever the status. app.js:41-42 has no try/catch. A 500 or 401 body such as {"error":"..."} is assigned to orders; renderStats then does `for (const o of orders)` over a non-iterable and throws, and the table keeps the old rows. There is no loading, error or empty state anywhere in index.html or app.js. Traced.
failing_case: The API returns 401 with a JSON object: console shows 'orders is not iterable', the cards and table stay as they were and the user sees no error. If the network drops, the fetch rejection is unhandled.
remediation: Check res.ok, throw with the status, catch in load(), and show a visible error with a retry; add loading and empty states.

title: Discount and 8.25% tax rules live inside a render function, and applying tax and discount to a stored total gives numbers that disagree with the table
evidence: app.js:9-17: pricing rules are in renderStats. The table (app.js:32) shows raw o.total while the stats multiply by 0.9 and 1.0825, so revenue never equals the sum of what is shown. Driven: 25 orders of $100 (one gold) gave $2695.43 revenue vs. $2500 shown in the table. Pending orders are ignored silently.
failing_case: Table rows add to $2500 for paid orders; the REVENUE card says $2695.43.
remediation: Move to one pure, tested function (netTotal(order)) that uses integer cents and is shared by table and stats; the server should own tax and discount.

title: Empty result divides by zero and displays $NaN
evidence: Driven: search that returns [] showed '$NaN AVG ORDER'. Also load() at app.js:41 crashes on a non-array error body (orders.slice / for-of).
failing_case: Type a query that matches no customer: the stats card shows $NaN.
remediation: Guard orders.length === 0 and show 0.00 or a dash plus an empty state.

title: Page count rounds down and is not reset when the filter changes
evidence: Driven: 25 orders shows 'of 2'; zero results after search shows 'Page 5 of 0'. load() (app.js:38-43) never resets page, so a new search while on page 3 shows an empty table.
failing_case: Go to page 2 of 2, type a search that returns 5 orders: the table is empty and the label says 'Page 2 of 0'.
remediation: Reset page to 1 in load(), use Math.ceil, and show an empty-state message when there are no rows.

title: Toast is not a live region, so the refund result is never announced
evidence: No role="status" or aria-live. app.js:51 sets textContent and display:block only. WCAG 4.1.3 (AA).
failing_case: A screen reader user clicks Refund and hears nothing, whether it worked or not.
remediation: Add role="status" (role="alert" for failures) to the container, present from page load, and set its text on change.

title: The toast pulses forever, never hides, and ignores prefers-reduced-motion
evidence: styles.css:20 sets an infinite scale animation; app.js:51 sets display:block and nothing ever hides the toast. No @media (prefers-reduced-motion) exists. WCAG 2.2.2 (A) for moving content over 5 s that cannot be stopped. Traced.
failing_case: After one refund the toast scales 1 to 1.05 every second for the rest of the session; users with vestibular disorders cannot stop it.
remediation: Remove the infinite animation, auto-dismiss or add a close button, and wrap any motion in a no-preference media query.
